newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent futures end weaker, hit by profit taking.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent futures end weaker, hit by profit taking.

text.p: IPE Brent futures ended at the lows of the day as profit taking and volatile NYMEX heating oil erased all of the day's gains in late business, traders said.

Front-month Brent was stuck in a range between $18.10-15 for much of the day after shrinking from early gains built on news of a Tehran-Bonn political row and cold U.S. weather but the contract was sold sharply lower through $18 into the close.
The May Brent contract last traded seven cents down at the day's low of $17.86 a barrel after making 27 cents to touch $18.20 in morning trade.

Brokers said reports that a new cold spell would affect the United States up to early next week and the Tehran-Bonn row gave a boost to the market in early trade, especially May gas oil, but the gains were under pressure in late business with NYMEX heating oil loosing over one cent a gallon.
They said technicals were also initially supportive with Brent and NYMEX crude seen creeping out of the oversold region until late bouts of profit talking set the market back.
Iran's diplomatic stand-off with the European Union put oil traders on alert and initially boosted prices on Friday amid concern that an escalation might threaten vital oil supplies.

However, European oil companies including France's Total and Anglo-Dutch oil giant Shell said on Friday they would not be deterred from investments in Iran despite a new crisis in relations between the European Union and Tehran.
Gas oil futures ended firmer but were also pulled back from early highs by profit taking into the close.

The May gas oil contract last traded $2.75 up at $163.25 a tonne after touching a high of $164.75 boosted in early trade by stronger crude and as cold U.S. weather boosted sentiment. --Colin Wooster, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7456
